title: PBL Builder Learner Profile
description: Describes one learner. This is the primary input to project design — the project is designed outward from this document. Lives in the YAML frontmatter of learners/<slug>/learner-profile.md.

schema_version.description: Schema version. Bump only on a breaking change.

learner.description: Use a first name or a pseudonym. Never a full name.

pronouns.description: e.g. 'she/her', 'they/them'. Omit if unknown — downstream text will use they/them.

jurisdiction.description: Standards jurisdiction. 'Multi-State' covers CCSS Math, CCSS ELA, NGSS, and C3 social studies. Otherwise a US state name, or a free-text label for non-US frameworks. Selects which set `pbl standards` searches.

subjects.description: Subject areas this project should cover.

standards_targets.description: What this learner actually needs to learn. Codes are validated against framework/standards/ by `pbl profile check` — a code that does not resolve is an error, not a warning.

framework.description: e.g. 'NGSS', 'CCSS.MATH', 'CCSS.ELA-LITERACY', 'C3', or a state framework name.

code.description: The official code, or exactly 'TBD' if it could not be verified. Never invent a code that looks real.

text.description: The standard's text, or a faithful paraphrase of what the learner must be able to do.

status.description: Where the learner is now. Drives milestone type: not-started gets direct instruction, developing gets application and critique, secure is used as leverage and not retaught.

success_skill_target.description: EXACTLY ONE skill. A project that assesses five success skills teaches none of them.

dimensions.description: Which rubric rows to teach and assess. Must match dimension ids in framework/success-skills/<skill>.yaml. One or two is better than three.

current_level.description: Where the learner sits now on the named dimensions.

evidence.description: What you observed that led to that level. Worth writing — it's what you compare against at the end.

interests.description: At least two SPECIFIC things. 'Reading' and 'sports' are rejected by `pbl profile check` — they produce generic projects. Write what you'd actually see them doing: 'rewatches the same three nature documentaries', 'takes apart broken electronics'.
examples: takes apart broken appliances to see inside
obsessed with the creek behind the house
draws detailed maps of imaginary places

strengths.description: Observable behaviors, not traits. 'Smart' and 'good student' are rejected. 'Notices when an argument contradicts itself' is useful.
examples: will redo a drawing five times to get it right
explains things clearly to younger kids

preferences.description: How this learner likes to work. Drives product selection and how much choice to offer.

product_modes.description: Ways of making things this learner is drawn to. Matched against the `modes` field of entries in framework/product-types.yaml to build the product menu.

work_mode.description: Preferred working arrangement. Affects who provides critique and how the support plan is written.

choice_appetite.description: How much open choice helps versus paralyses. Low does not mean no choice — it means a narrow menu that widens as they gain footing.

audience_comfort.description: Comfort presenting to people. Low means build a comfort_ramp in the plan. It NEVER means drop the public audience.

dislikes.description: Worth recording. 'Hates writing by hand' changes product choice more than most strengths do.

needs.description: Functional descriptions only — what helps them learn. Never diagnoses, IEP contents, medication, or assessment scores. Tags here are matched against framework/scaffolds.yaml, and every populated need must have at least one scaffold in the resulting plan.

reading_level.description: Relative to grade, in plain terms.
examples: about two years below grade level
reads well above grade but avoids long texts

executive_function.description: Task initiation, planning, time, working memory, task-switching.

language_supports.description: Academic vocabulary, English language development, expressive or receptive language.

accommodations.description: Practical accommodations already in place. Free text — these come from you, not from a fixed list.
examples: text-to-speech for anything over a page

sensory_or_physical.description: Anything affecting how they access the work or a venue. Relevant to field experiences and presentation logistics.

none.description: Set true to state explicitly that there are no additional needs. Distinguishes 'nothing to note' from 'not filled in yet'.

pbl_experience.description: How much project-based work they've done. Sets scaffold density and how fast choice widens. 'none' plus low choice_appetite means a tightly structured first project — and that's fine.

adults_available.description: Who can support, and roughly how much. Determines what the support_plan can promise.
examples: tutor 2x/week for 90 min, no support between sessions

weekly_hours.description: Hours per week available for this project.

community.description: The local context the project can draw on and give back to. This is where authenticity comes from — be concrete.
examples: small farm town, creek runs behind the property, active watershed council

resources.description: What's actually available: tools, spaces, people, transport, a library card.

total_weeks.description: Weeks available. Under 3 is very hard to do well — sustained inquiry needs time.

budget.description: Money available for materials, if any.

travel_ok.description: Can the project include going places?

tech_available.description: Devices, software, connectivity. Constrains product type more than people expect.

hard_dates.description: Fixed dates to plan around — a co-op showcase, a council meeting, a trip.
examples: watershed council meets the first Tuesday of each month

goals_from_adult.description: What YOU want out of this project, in your own words. Often the most useful field in the file — it surfaces the real goal, which is sometimes not academic at all.
examples: I want him to finish something he's proud of. He starts a lot and finishes almost nothing.

status.description: Profile lifecycle. `ready` means it has passed `pbl profile check`.

updated.description: ISO date last revised. Profiles go stale — a year-old reading level is fiction.

grade.description: Grade level as a string. Matches the gradeLevel values in the standards data.

success_skill.description: One of the five success skills. See framework/success-skills/.

skill_level.description: The four performance levels used across all success skills rubrics.

product_mode.description: Ways of making something. Deliberately about the ACT of making, not the artifact — a learner who likes 'build-physical' will take to a model or a prototype regardless of subject.

need_tag.description: Functional need tags. Each maps to scaffolds in framework/scaffolds.yaml. Deliberately functional, never diagnostic — 'working-memory' not a disorder name.
